cards.explanation: The answer is prophets. Paul says God promised the gospel beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures. So the good news was written down long before Paul ever picked up a pen. Some of us can't plan a cookie batch an hour ahead, friends, and this was promised way back.

The answer is David. Paul says God's Son was a descendant of David according to the flesh. That's the human side of the family line. Paul puts it right at the start of his letter, and I bet he wants Rome to hear it.

The answer is by His resurrection from the dead. Paul says that through the Spirit of holiness, Jesus was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead. Of everything Paul could have pointed to, he points there. Then he gives the name: Jesus Christ our Lord.

The answer is to call the Gentiles to obedience from faith. Paul says we received grace and apostleship to call all those among the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith. Gentiles are people who aren't Jews. So the call goes out wide, friends, and it's an obedience that comes from faith.
The answer is True. Paul says to the believers in Rome, "And you also are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ." (Romans 1:6) He counts them right in with the called ones, friends.

The answer is God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. That's who Paul says grace and peace come from. He puts both names right there in his greeting. I'd take a letter that opens like that over a coupon flyer any day.

The answer is that their faith is being proclaimed all over the world. Paul says he thanks God for all of them because of that. News about their faith is traveling. Paul takes that and turns it into a thank-you to God.

The answer is that by God's will he may come to Rome. Paul says he's asking in his prayers at all times that now at last, by God's will, he may succeed in coming to them. He keeps bringing it to God. I think a man who prays that long for a visit really wants to get there.

The answer is True. Paul says he and the believers in Rome may be "…mutually encouraged by each other’s faith." (Romans 1:12) So the encouragement goes both ways, friends. It isn't just him encouraging them.

The answer is that he has been prevented until now. Paul says he planned to come to them often, but has been prevented from visiting until now. The text doesn't say what stopped him, so I won't guess. He just tells them he kept planning.

The answer is eager. Paul says he's obligated to Greeks and non-Greeks, to the wise and the foolish, and that's why he's so eager to preach the gospel to the believers in Rome too. I'm eager when a fresh batch comes out of the oven. Paul's eager about the gospel.

The answer is that it is the power of God for salvation. Paul says he isn't ashamed of the gospel because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes. That's his reason, plain and simple, friends. It's power that comes from God.
The answer is False. Paul says the gospel is the power of God for salvation "…to everyone who believes, first to the Jew, then to the Greek." (Romans 1:16) The word he uses is everyone, friends.

The answer is faith. Paul says the gospel reveals the righteousness of God that comes by faith from start to finish. Then he adds what is written: "The righteous will live by faith." That one word carries the whole verse, bakers.
